title: Live at the Egyptian Theatre
summary: DVDASA records a live pre-film show at the Egyptian Theatre in Los Angeles with David Choe, Asa Akira, Critter Fleming, Valentine, Money Mark, Bobby NAMBLA and a quiet introduction by Quiet C. The show begins with Asa's wins at the televised Sex Awards and discussion of directing women, performer chemistry and the difference between genuine desire and competitive on-set dynamics. Projected pornography and stage sightlines make portions visual-only; the transcript cannot fully represent what the audience sees. The cast introduces Money Mark, Valentine's Yakuza Boy persona, Bobby's hockey team and a newly arrived player. A Comic-Con audience member returns after licking Bobby's open hand lesion. The lesion reportedly recurred after treatment and the fan says he did not develop visible growths; this anecdote does not establish safety or diagnose either person. David then gives the clearest provenance account for DVDASA: after a 24-hour Reddit/AMA-style November 2 event involving live video replies, multiple platform accounts and videos were deleted. He says the loss motivated a site the group could control. This directly connects the November 2 recordings to the show's archival mission. He previews another November 2 event without a settled platform or program. Audience questions cover love versus sex, zines, the Mexico City show, a Beastie Boys bomb-threat concert story, the return of Thumbs Up!, hitchhiking, food recommendations, ESL, uncertain careers, relationships and private partners. Money Mark's Beastie Boys story is a first-person tour recollection; the promoter-sabotage explanation remains attributed rather than independently verified. David's advice to a nineteen-year-old includes hitchhiking, sneaking into venues and even airplanes. It is autobiographical/provocative advice, not a safety or legal guide, and the flight example is especially dangerous. A consenting adult audience member and Asa touch breasts and kiss onstage; later another established couple voluntarily performs a closing make-out. Momentary stage consent does not authorize republication of private images, contact details or identity trails. A separate nineteen-year-old audience member describes virginity, oral sex, pornography and difficulty with intimacy. The cast sexualizes her, invites audience attention and gives contradictory advice, including concealing virginity until after sex. She states adulthood, but remains a private young adult; her city, ethnicity, studies and sexual disclosures must not be composed into an identity. The cast's repeated 'always fuck' rule is comic relationship philosophy, not consent guidance. The most useful final segment asks what friends love and dislike about David. Answers describe generosity, friendship-first loyalty, interruption, pressure, high expectations and continuous post-show debriefs. David says the program remains amateur, unprepared and open to change, while expressing a desire for an uncut record he controls. The event closes with voluntary stage intimacy, Bobby dancing, the cast sign-off and a transition to Why Don't You Play in Hell?
